text:
jess: Quick heads-up — final publish for py/ts SDKs scheduled 14:00 PT today. Need: pin confirmation for py wheels + TS disttag, final release notes, and deprecation blurb for legacy sync client.

owen: I can handle the TS disttag pin. planning to cut canary at 13:30 PT and shadow traffic for 15m.

release-bot: [automated] canary publish started for @owen (pkg: sdk-ts, tag: canary-2026-06-01)

chi: For the deprecation blurb — do we prefer a gentle deprec (30d) or immediate soft-deprec with compatibility shim? Product asked for 60d but legal may want docs copy.

jess: Let's do 45d soft deprec + shim for one major. Put exact wording in release notes: "legacy sync client deprecated; use async client v2; shim available for backwards compat". I'll draft.

owen: pin plan: TS disttag -> set `stable` -> canary -> GA. If canary looks good at 13:45, I'll flip to stable at 14:05.

release-bot: [automated] canary publish succeeded (pkg: sdk-ts, checksum: sha256:abcd1234)

deploy-bot: rollouts initiated: py wheels canary -> 10% users, ts disttag shadow -> enabled

ana: @jess quick: Do we need to bump major for py wheels because of shim removal?

jess: No major bump now — minor with deprecation note. We'll reserve major for shim removal later.

owen: Filing release notes PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/612

ana: seeing a warning on the py wheel checksum after canary: local checksum `sha256:abcd1234` vs index `sha256:abcd1235` — small mismatch.

jess: Ugh. Which platform/builder?

ana: linux-x86_64 wheel built in pipeline #4823.

release-bot: [automated] build #4823 finished: wheel artifact uploaded -> s3://redwood-builds/py/wheels/4823/sdk-1.9.0-cp39.whl (size: 4.1MB)

own: If checksum mismatch, we should pause stable flip. Keep canary live and hold the GA cut.

jess: Agreed — hold flip. Owen, don't pin `stable` yet. Chi, please open a build reverify ticket and run `pip install --no-cache-dir` against the wheel URL.

chi: On it. Running `pip install --no-cache-dir https://s3.redwood/sdk-1.9.0-cp39.whl` and checking hashes.

chi: Confirmed mismatch locally. Re-ran build step with same commit -> got same checksum as index (sha256:abcd1235). Looks like artifact duplication from prior run (old artifact lingering).

jess: So likely stale artifact upload. Plan: we tag a fresh build, verify checksum, then re-run canary. If fresh build matches the index, then flip to stable. If not, rollback to previous release.

own: For rollback criteria: any mismatch OR >3% error rate on canary OR increased median latency by >50ms -> immediate rollback and pinback to previous disttag.

jess: Documented. I'll update PR with rollback criteria and deprecation copy.

release-bot: [automated] tagging new build queue started (builder: ci-runner-03)

deploy-bot: paused GA flip per @jess request. Canary remains at 10%.

ana: new build uploaded: checksum sha256:abcd5678, build #4824.

chi: Verified `sha256:abcd5678` locally, pip install clean.

own: canary shadow looks clean — no errors reported for 20m, latencies stable. I'd say proceed to flip at 14:10 PT.

jess: Proceed but keep pins reversible. Owen, when you flip, don't remove the old disttag — set stable->new and keep `stable-previous` pointing to old. Also make a quick rollback script: `scripts/pin-back.sh <pkg> <old-disttag>`.

own: Copy. Preparing the flip.

deploy-bot: [automated] disttag change queued: sdk-ts stable -> canary-2026-06-01 (operator: owen)

release-bot: [automated] disttag update succeeded. stable now points to canary-2026-06-01

ana: popping a small post-publish smoke: `import redwood; redwood.__version__` returns 1.9.0 for py on my env. All good. :white_check_mark:

jess: Great. Final checklist: 1) merge release notes PR (owen) 2) publish release blog with deprec blurb (jess) 3) create support FAQ (chi) 4) schedule deprec email 45d out (ana).

own: Merged release notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/612#mergecommit

jess: Thanks team. We'll monitor the first 24h and revert if rollback criteria hit. Posting final release announcement at 14:30 PT. :party-parrot:

release-bot: [automated] release published: v1.9.0 (notes: https://docs.redwood/releases/1.9.0)

jess: Closing thread — follow-ups in the release PR.
